section_summary: This section follows opposition to the proposed deconcentration of Tokyo Shibaura Electric Company through union petitions, a review board recommendation, a proposed order, and later diplomatic reporting. It also contains a Yokosuka union petition about political affiliation affidavits, State Department discussions of Japanese labor policy, and memoranda on Japanese participation in international labor organizations.

subfiles.title: Opposition of Union to Deconcentration of Tokyo Shibaura Electric Company
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports union opposition to the proposed Toshiba deconcentration order and the review board’s response.
subfiles.summary: The Toshiba federation argues that disposing of plants will disrupt production and employment and that the permitted merger contradicts deconcentration. Roy S. Campbell defends the plan. Union representatives also criticize the unclear lines of authority among Occupation and Japanese agencies.

subfiles.title: Petition of the Federation of Toshiba Unions
subfiles.from: Tomoki Yamashita, Federation of Toshiba Unions
subfiles.about: Opposes detachment of 28 Toshiba factories and laboratories.
subfiles.summary: The federation says Toshiba’s plants are interdependent, vital production will suffer, the Rolling Stock merger increases concentration, and 7,000 workers may lose jobs. It proposes dividing heavy and light electrical operations instead.

subfiles.title: Deconcentration Review Board recommendation on Tokyo Shibaura Denki
subfiles.from: Roy S. Campbell, Deconcentration Review Board
subfiles.about: Recommends plant disposal instead of dividing Toshiba into successor companies.
subfiles.summary: The board finds Toshiba excessively concentrated but rejects a proposed five-company breakup. It recommends disposal of specified plants while permitting Toshiba to retain interests in Toshiba Sharyo and Kyodo Tatemono.

subfiles.title: Proposed Order of Reorganization: Tokyo Shibaura Denki
subfiles.from: Holding Company Liquidation Commission; Tadao Sasayama, chairman
subfiles.about: Orders disposal of specified Toshiba facilities and sets terms for merger and financial reorganization.
subfiles.summary: The commission finds excessive concentration, orders supervised plant disposal, permits reacquisition of Toshiba Sharyo shares for a merger, and requires a financial reorganization plan.

subfiles.title: Federation of Toshiba Unions petition to the Secretary of State
subfiles.from: T. Ishikawa, Federation of Toshiba Unions
subfiles.about: Challenges the proposed Toshiba plant disposals and their expected effect on workers.
subfiles.summary: The petition argues that separating 28 facilities will damage production and threaten thousands of jobs. It questions the Rolling Stock merger and suggests separate heavy and light electrical businesses.

subfiles.title: Moscow telegram on Japanese attendance at Soviet trade union congress
subfiles.about: Reports Soviet press coverage of MacArthur’s refusal to allow Japanese union representatives at a Soviet congress.
subfiles.summary: Reports a Soviet press account and statement on the denied visit.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo despatch 229 and international labor meetings
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP’s refusal to allow Japanese non-Communist unionists to attend the Indore conference.
subfiles.summary: SCAP feared discriminatory treatment would provoke Communist charges.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Labor Problems in Japan
subfiles.about: Records Robert T. Amis’s views on SCAP labor staffing, stabilization, union politics, and labor law revisions.
subfiles.summary: Amis expects labor unrest under economic stabilization and discusses the strengths and weaknesses of anti-Communist union groups. He explains proposed union law revisions, employer support for unions, and his view that government enterprise workers should regain the right to strike.

subfiles.title: United Metal Workers petition on Yokosuka union affidavits
subfiles.from: Jiro Wada, United Metal Workers of Japan
subfiles.about: Protests a Yokosuka naval order requiring union officers to sign political affiliation affidavits.
subfiles.summary: Wada argues that refusing to sign should not expose union leaders to adverse assumptions or penalties.

subfiles.title: Restricted Information Sheet for Yokosuka union officers
subfiles.about: Requests personal, employment, union, political affiliation, and travel information.
subfiles.summary: Blank questionnaire delivered to Yokosuka unions through the police.

subfiles.title: Certification for Yokosuka union officers
subfiles.about: Requires signers to deny association with Communist, fascist, totalitarian, or subversive organizations.
subfiles.summary: Blank certification requires disclosure of later changes and warns against false statements.

subfiles.title: Interview of Yokosuka labor union leaders with U.S. Fleet Activities
subfiles.about: Records naval officials’ explanation of the affidavit requirement and union leaders’ questions.
subfiles.summary: Naval representatives say union officers may decline to sign but also state that failure to submit signed forms by the deadline will be treated as evidence of prohibited organizational connections. Questions address who must submit forms, how later changes are reported, and the consequences of false certification.

subfiles.title: Interview with the SCAP Labor Section about Yokosuka affidavits
subfiles.about: Asks whether the Yokosuka affidavit demand reflects SCAP labor policy.
subfiles.summary: A Labor Section representative calls the requirement tentative, says it is under investigation, and tentatively advises the unionists against signing.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Australian labor resolution before the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Recommends opposing an Australian proposal extending trade union principles to Japanese government workers.
subfiles.summary: Reports a Steering Committee vote and recommends instructions to General McCoy.

subfiles.title: Instruction to United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Authorizes a vote against Australia’s proposal on Japanese government workers’ labor rights.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes the U.S. member to vote against proposal SC-318/19.

subfiles.title: Federation of Toshiba Labor Unions follow-up petition
subfiles.from: Tomoki Yamashita, Federation of Toshiba Labor Unions
subfiles.about: Renews the federation’s request to reconsider the Toshiba deconcentration directive.
subfiles.summary: The federation cites Diet hearings, press debate, and concern among other unions. It argues that the proposed directive remains legally and economically flawed and asks for further consideration before a final order is issued.

subfiles.title: Deconcentration of Tokyo Shibaura Electric Company
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, United States Political Adviser’s Mission
subfiles.about: Reports approval of the Toshiba deconcentration order and continuing labor opposition.
subfiles.summary: The commission approved the order without amendment. The federation planned protest and appeal, while Diet testimony and press discussion questioned whether the order served deconcentration or industrial rationalization.

subfiles.title: Makoto Kan petition on Toshiba deconcentration
subfiles.from: Makoto Kan, Congress of Industrial Unions of Japan
subfiles.about: Opposes the draft Toshiba order as harmful to production and employment.
subfiles.summary: Kan urges action before an unchanged final order is issued.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Paul Jackson as possible labor attaché
subfiles.to: W. J. Sebald and Max Bishop
subfiles.about: Relays a SCAP Labor Division officer’s reservations about Paul Jackson.
subfiles.summary: Green questions Jackson’s usefulness as a labor attaché after speaking with Hepler.

subfiles.title: Request of Chinese Member, Allied Council for Japan, for Information Regarding Reorganization of Tokyo Shibaura Electric Company
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards the Chinese Allied Council member’s inquiry and the American reply.
subfiles.summary: Notes the status of Toshiba and other pending deconcentration cases.

subfiles.title: Chinese member’s request for information on Toshiba reorganization
subfiles.from: Office of the Member for China, Allied Council for Japan
subfiles.to: Office of the Chairman and United States Member, Allied Council for Japan
subfiles.about: Seeks facts and comment on Toshiba’s order and the wider deconcentration program.
subfiles.summary: After receiving union petitions, the Chinese member requests information to assess the order’s legal, economic, and social implications.

subfiles.title: Reply to General Chu on Toshiba and economic deconcentration
subfiles.about: Explains the Toshiba order, appeal procedure, and progress of Japan’s deconcentration program.
subfiles.summary: Huston outlines the planned disposal of 27 plants and a laboratory, addresses union fears and the Toshiba Sharyo merger, and lists completed and pending company cases. He places the order within SCAP’s wider anti-trust program.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Tokyo despatch 423
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Chinese member’s inquiry and Huston’s reply on Toshiba.
subfiles.summary: Notes the order’s expected effective date and summarizes deconcentration progress.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Japanese Supreme Court labor decision
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Supreme Court ruling against an employer’s dismissal of union workers.
subfiles.summary: Calls the ruling liberal while noting that its wider application remains uncertain.

subfiles.title: Office memorandum on telegrams to Far Eastern Commission capitals
subfiles.about: Discusses whether to send additional telegrams concerning Far Eastern Commission policy.
subfiles.summary: Reports one telegram sent and suggests similar messages to London and Ottawa.

subfiles.title: Australian Proposal in FEC on Labor Policy in Japan
subfiles.about: Recommends directly explaining U.S. opposition to the Australian labor proposal in Canberra.
subfiles.summary: Reports an expected vote and attaches a proposed telegram to Canberra.

subfiles.title: Invitation to Non-Communist Labor Unions of Japan to Join New World Labor Organization
subfiles.about: Argues for allowing Japanese non-Communist unions to participate in a new international labor organization.
subfiles.summary: Swayze reviews SCAP’s earlier refusals and argues that international participation could counter Communist influence and strengthen Japanese unions through contacts with foreign labor leaders. The memorandum continues beyond this section.
